title: GJ 3323 paired velocities reject independent Gaussian formal errors but permit a persistent error model
abstract: We test whether quoted marginal errors explain the difference between two HARPS-RVBank version 02 velocity products for GJ 3323. For 121 accepted exposures in two seasons, we use the largest possible same-exposure difference variance, the square of the sum of the quoted errors. After two season offsets, the squared residual score is 341.269 for rank 119. Under independent Gaussian exposure errors, any within-pair covariance gives a tail bound of 2.48e-23. The moment scale is 1.693. Both seasons and a control that removes the two known period waves retain this conditional failure. The conclusion depends on time covariance. Gaussian independent-block bounds are 0.0134 for fixed 10-day blocks and 0.0935 for 30-day blocks. With unrestricted time dependence, a valid persistent Gaussian error construction gives a tail of 0.0918 at the observed score. Thus this score cannot give a uniform 5 percent rejection of that broad null class. The construction is a mathematical counterexample, not a measured instrument model. No planet is confirmed or excluded. The package includes original code, proof, aggregate results and a figure. External data and record-level derivatives are excluded; exact source hashes and separate-scratch reproduction steps are supplied.

display.caption: The moment scale exceeds one with maximum paired-error variance. Gaussian tail bounds weaken when the assumed independent blocks are longer. These are conditional error-model tests, not planet probabilities.
